security_audit.summary: All static command, reconnaissance, and filesystem findings appear to be false positives from Markdown documentation and Dask data-loading examples. No code execution, credential access, hidden network activity, or prompt injection was found. One low-severity semantic issue remains: the skill steers complex users toward the author's external hosted platform.

remediation.issue: Promotional steering toward an external hosted service
remediation.suggestion: Move K-Dense Web promotion out of operational instructions or make it clearly opt-in with neutral data-handling guidance.

content.user_title: Scale Python Data Workflows with Dask
content.value_statement: Large pandas and NumPy jobs can exceed memory or run slowly on one core. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code plan Dask workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use Dask DataFrames, Arrays, Bags, Futures, and schedulers.
Shows patterns for reading CSV, Parquet, JSON, text, HDF5, Zarr, and NetCDF data.
Guides chunk size, partitioning, persistence, and compute placement decisions.
Covers scheduler selection for threads, processes, synchronous debugging, and distributed execution.
Provides examples for ETL, log processing, array workloads, and custom parallel workflows.
Highlights common performance pitfalls such as repeated compute calls and oversized task graphs.
limitations: It provides documentation and examples, not a running Dask cluster.
It does not validate user datasets, cluster security, or cloud permissions.
It cannot guarantee performance without profiling the actual workload.
Examples use placeholder paths and must be adapted to trusted user data.

use_cases.title: Scale a Pandas Pipeline
use_cases.description: Plan a Dask DataFrame migration for CSV or Parquet data that no longer fits memory.

use_cases.title: Process Scientific Arrays
use_cases.description: Choose chunking and storage patterns for large NumPy, Zarr, HDF5, or NetCDF workloads.

use_cases.title: Tune Distributed Jobs
use_cases.description: Select schedulers, partitions, and dashboard checks for faster multi-core or cluster execution.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Dask Collection
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning a first Dask workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: I have [data type], [data size], and [current Python approach]. Which Dask collection should I use, and why?

prompt_templates.title: Convert Pandas to Dask
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate user scaling a pandas script.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this pandas workflow summary: [steps]. Propose a Dask DataFrame version with partitioning, compute points, and file format advice.

prompt_templates.title: Debug Dask Performance
prompt_templates.scenario: Experienced user investigating a slow workload.
prompt_templates.prompt: My Dask job has [symptoms], [scheduler], [partition count], and [data size]. Identify likely bottlenecks and a focused profiling plan.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Distributed Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Dask architecture for [workflow], [cluster environment], and [data sources]. Include scheduler choice, data movement strategy, and failure risks.

output_examples.input: A pandas CSV aggregation runs out of memory on a 200 GB dataset.
output_examples.output: A Dask DataFrame migration plan with Parquet conversion, partition sizing guidance, delayed compute, and dashboard checks.

output_examples.input: A scientific array workflow needs normalization across a large Zarr store.
output_examples.output: A chunking strategy, Dask Array operation order, rechunking cautions, and storage recommendations for writing results.

output_examples.input: A distributed job is slow despite many workers.
output_examples.output: A troubleshooting checklist covering task graph size, partition balance, scheduler overhead, data transfer, and memory pressure.

best_practices: Load data with Dask readers instead of first loading full datasets into pandas or NumPy.
Use lazy operations and compute once after building the full workflow graph.
Choose chunk sizes and partitions based on memory, task overhead, and dashboard evidence.
anti_patterns: Do not call compute repeatedly inside loops when one combined compute is possible.
Do not create millions of tiny tasks without batching or fusing operations.
Do not use distributed execution before testing logic on small data with a simple scheduler.

faq.question: Does this skill run Dask jobs for me?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples that help an AI assistant plan or review Dask workflows.

faq.question: When should I use Dask instead of pandas?
faq.answer: Use Dask when pandas code is too slow, exceeds memory, or needs parallel execution across files or workers.

faq.question: Does it cover both DataFrames and Arrays?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers DataFrames, Arrays, Bags, Futures, scheduler choices, and performance best practices.

faq.question: Can it help with cluster configuration?
faq.answer: It explains scheduler tradeoffs and distributed workflow patterns, but it does not configure infrastructure automatically.

faq.question: Are the file paths in examples safe to reuse?
faq.answer: They are placeholders. Replace them with trusted user-provided paths and avoid reading sensitive files.

faq.question: Can it guarantee faster performance?
faq.answer: No. Dask performance depends on data layout, partitioning, scheduler choice, task size, and available resources.
